name: LV25-P_SP5
title: LV 25-P/SP5: closed-loop Hall-effect voltage transducer, 10 to 1500 V nominal, 10 mA primary, current output
summary: A compensated (closed-loop) Hall-effect transducer that measures DC, AC and pulsed voltages with the measured circuit isolated from the output. A user-fitted series resistor R1 turns the voltage under test into a primary current of up to 10 mA r.m.s. nominal (0 to ±14 mA range) through the primary winding; the turns ratio of 2500 : 1000 gives a secondary current of 25 mA nominal, delivered from pin M into a measuring resistor RM. It runs from ±15 V (±5 %), reaches ±0.8 % total error at the nominal current and 25 °C, and suits nominal voltages from 10 to 1500 V. Insulation is tested at 4.2 kV r.m.s.; the PCB-mount case has two primary and three secondary pins and works from -40 to +85 °C.

notes: The label on the top of the case carries the model on one line and the SP number with the date code on a second line; the case material is marked >PBT<.

The case has no 0 V pin; in the connection, RM returns to the 0 V terminal.

circuits.title: Connection
circuits.description: The voltage under test is applied between the +HT and -HT terminals. R1 in series with the +HT pin sets the primary current, which returns from -HT. The transducer runs from +UC on pin + and -UC on pin -; its output pin M drives the secondary current IS through an ammeter and the measuring resistor RM to the 0 V terminal.

operation.text: Closed-loop Hall-effect transducer. The part itself senses a current: a resistor R1, fitted by the user in series with the primary winding, converts the voltage to be measured into a proportional primary current. The output current IS is isolated from the measured circuit and follows DC, AC and pulsed voltages.
Accuracy is best at the nominal primary current, so R1 is sized to pass 10 mA at the nominal voltage. At 250 V, 25 kΩ (10 mA) gives ±0.8 % of UPN and 50 kΩ (5 mA) gives ±1.6 % of UPN, both at +25 °C.
Nominal voltages from 10 to 1500 V are the recommended range. It allows for the insulation and for the primary winding resistance, which has to stay small beside R1 to keep thermal drift low.
IS is positive when the measured voltage UP is applied to the positive high-voltage terminal (+HT).

Insulation is tested at Ud = 4.2 kV r.m.s. (50 Hz, 1 min), and also at 4 kV DC for 5 minutes. Impulse withstand is 16 kV (1.2/50 µs); creepage and clearance between the primary pins and the secondary pins are both at least 19.5 mm.

The secondary side belongs in limited-energy circuits as defined by IEC 61010-1. In use, parts of the module such as the primary connections and the supply can be at a hazardous voltage, so the transducer is built into equipment with its live parts out of reach, for instance behind a protective housing or shield, and the mains supply must have a means of disconnection.

Under the UL 508 recognition the end equipment must enclose the device, and its terminals are not rated for field wiring. It mounts on the end product's printed board, which needs a CTI of 100 or more; an uncoated board limits it to pollution degree 2. It sits on the load side of any line filter. The low-voltage side is fed from an isolated source with no direct link back to the primary apart from the grounding. The solder joint between a primary coil pin and the primary bus bar may not exceed 100 °C.

Fitting follows LEM's generic transducer mounting rules, document ANE120504, unless this part's data states otherwise. Primary pins are 0.635 mm square, secondary pins ⌀ 1 mm; the recommended PCB hole is ⌀ 1.2 mm.
The insulating plastic case is recognised to UL 94-V0.
Listed advantages: excellent accuracy, very good linearity, low temperature drift, optimised response time, wide frequency bandwidth and high immunity to external interference.
Listed applications: single- and three-phase inverters, propulsion and braking choppers, propulsion and auxiliary converters, and battery chargers, in railway equipment both fixed and on board.
